metrics.compose_additional: Released generators force the constraint during decoding and so do not report fragment satisfaction. COMPOSE can propose outside the constraint, so it must additionally report constraint validity and use STRICT benchmark validity (chemically valid AND constraint satisfied) as its headline validity.
metrics.distance_central: mean Tanimoto distance from the parent drug to unique valid completions; Morgan radius 2, 1024 bits. GenMol reports it; InVirtuoGen's main table omits it.
metrics.diversity: mean pairwise Tanimoto distance over unique valid molecules; Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits, no chirality
metrics.quality: unique valid molecules with QED >= 0.6 AND SA <= 4, divided by ALL 100 attempts (note the denominator)
metrics.uniqueness: unique valid canonical molecules / valid molecules
metrics.validity: parseable (and connected) outputs / 100 attempts, averaged over drugs

pilot_implemented.design: 10 motif-extension prompts x 12 variant indices = 120 attempts. Abstentions are scored as empty samples so they lower validity rather than shrinking the denominator. Metrics computed by the repo's official evaluator (evaluate_prompt) with expected_samples=12.
pilot_implemented.quality_note: Mean quality 0.0917 (11 of 120 attempts pass QED >= 0.6 and SA <= 4). Appending an n-alkyl chain makes no attempt at drug-likeness, so this is expected and is likewise a proposal-law property, not an executor property.

uniqueness_ceiling.attribution: This is a property of a deliberately generic PLACEHOLDER proposal law, NOT a limit of the executor, the constraint checker, or the program representation. Zero abstentions over 120 attempts shows the executor never refused.
uniqueness_ceiling.cause: MEASURED AND READ FROM SOURCE, not inferred: fragment_constrained_runner._single_fragment_plan sets chain_length = 1 + variant_index % 3 for motif extension, so the variant law emits exactly three distinct completions (a 1-, 2- or 3-carbon chain) and then repeats.
uniqueness_ceiling.finding: Uniqueness is exactly 3/12 = 0.25 on EVERY prompt, with zero variance.
uniqueness_ceiling.projection_INFERRED: At the released 100-sample budget the same law would score uniqueness ~3%, versus 66.8-99.4% for the published baselines. Marked INFERRED: it is arithmetic on the observed period-3 law, not a measured 100-sample run.

pilot_implemented.why_this_one: Easiest of the five: exactly one retained fragment carrying exactly one declared attachment site, so it needs neither an inter-component bridge (linker design / scaffold morphing) nor an invented growth site (superstructure generation).

reproducibility_caveats_from_released_co: InVirtuoGen builds superstructure attachment prompts with random.choice BEFORE seeding, and does not persist them, so byte-exact replay of its superstructure conditioning is impossible from the release alone. The ten underlying core substructures are static and are what the COMPOSE adapter binds.

purpose: Scoped reconnaissance: is the SAFE/GenMol fragment-constrained benchmark free for COMPOSE, or does it need executor redesign?

state_semantics_check.detail: The runner never rebuilds a state by re-parsing SMILES into smiles_to_molecular_graph; it constructs padded sources (SLOTS = 48) and decodes committed states from the executor receipt. The atom_insert family is therefore present in the legal support, which matters because atom_insert is the primary operation all five tasks depend on.
state_semantics_check.reason: That preflight compares a TRAINED MODEL's realized legal-family census against a corpus-recorded census for the same source. This path has neither a trained model nor a compiler-recorded census, so it cannot be run here as specified.
state_semantics_check.substitute_check_performed: MEASURED the underlying invariant it protects directly: every committed state in every proposal was decoded with decode_state (rewrite/trace_shard) and carries 48 slots against 12-13 real atoms, i.e. free slots are present.

task_to_compose_mapping.executor_changes_required: NONE. All five tasks are expressed with two already-supported executor rules: atom_insert and cycle_close.
task_to_compose_mapping.measurement_basis: MEASURED: executor rules, primitive counts and block counts extracted from the real execution receipts of an independent 50-prompt panel re-run this session.
task_to_compose_mapping.retained_region_semantics: A retained region is expressed address-free: the adapter strips the dummy atoms to form a core query, remembers the neighbouring core roles, and requires every declared site to gain an external heavy-atom neighbour. Isotope labels are never used as atom addresses. Fragment locks are re-checked in EVERY committed state after the fragment's construction completes, not only at the endpoint.

linker_design.consequence: This is the one task where COMPOSE's connectivity invariant forces a genuinely different formulation than a sequence model's mask-and-infill. It is expressible with existing primitives, but it is the structurally hardest of the five.
linker_design.key_design_point: COMPOSE's committed non-null states must be COMPLETE CONNECTED molecules, so it can never hold the disconnected fragment pair. Instead it takes the LARGER retained fragment as the connected source and builds the bridge plus the entire second fragment atom-by-atom as ONE dependency-aware program (block 0 = generic_linker_path, block 1 = retained_fragment_construction, dependency 0->1). cycle_close appears where the second fragment contains a ring that must be closed after its atoms exist. Every intermediate state is validated and connected.

superstructure_generation.caveat: No dummy site is supplied, so the generator must CHOOSE where to grow. The v1 panel abstained once here (Futibatinib) because the site selector chose an atom bearing an explicit chiral hydrogen and the generic extension was over-valent; v2 restricts the site to a replaceable IMPLICIT hydrogen and completes 10/10. That was a runner defect, not an unsupported prompt.

free_already: MEASURED: all five task labels execute unchanged through the existing Editing-V2 executor using only atom_insert and cycle_close.
MEASURED: 50/50 prompts complete with 100% constraint satisfaction and 100% exact-valid execution, reproducibly and byte-identically.
MEASURED: 120/120 motif-extension attempts complete with 100% strict benchmark validity and zero abstentions.
Already built: typed prompt loading, address-free constraint checking, official metric denominators, fingerprint settings, provenance pinning and fail-closed schema/count drift handling.
verdict.is_the_benchmark_free_for_compose: SUBSTANTIALLY YES on the chemistry, program and constraint layers; NO as a publishable comparator result yet.
not_free: There is no SAMPLER. The proposal law is deterministic and period-3, so uniqueness, diversity and quality are placeholder numbers that cannot be compared to SAFE-GPT, GenMol or InVirtuoGen.
Closing that gap means conditioning the existing learned model / controller on the retained region to sample diverse completions. That is controller work, explicitly out of scope for this recon.
A publishable run additionally needs a self-hashed scored-launch contract, 100 attempts per prompt and three declared seeds.
verdict.recommendation: DO NOT PARK. The expensive and risky parts (exact-executor coverage of all five tasks, address-free constraint semantics, official metric fidelity, frozen provenance) are done and independently verified. The remaining work is a single well-scoped piece: sample completions from the learned model conditioned on the retained region instead of enumerating a generic chain. Budget the benchmark as controller-conditioning work, not as chemistry or executor work.
verdict.risk_flag: The honest headline risk is QUALITY, not validity. COMPOSE will trivially report ~100% strict validity (it cannot emit an invalid or constraint-violating molecule), but the published tables are won on quality and diversity, which depend entirely on the sampler that does not yet exist. A 100%-validity row with 3% uniqueness would be a worse look than not running the benchmark.
